# Café Start-Up Compliance Research: Westminster, Manchester & Edinburgh

## Executive Summary

Opening a small café as a sole trader in any of the three locations triggers requirements across six compliance categories: (1) business registration, (2) operating licence, (3) tax registration, (4) premises and safety, (5) sector-specific rules, and (6) renewals and ongoing filings. The core obligations are substantially similar across all three places — food business registration with the local authority at least 28 days before trading (free and cannot be refused), Self Assessment registration with HMRC, fire risk assessment, food safety management (HACCP), and allergen information — but Scotland introduces a mandatory Food Hygiene Information Scheme (FHIS) display obligation, different business rates rules, and a distinct Late Hours Catering licence regime administered by City of Edinburgh Council. Premises licences for alcohol or late-night hot food are **not required** on the stated facts (no alcohol, no hot food after 23:00). Overall operational timelines are **UNKNOWN** because no official source publishes an end-to-end approval window; the only published minimum is the 28-day food business registration advance-notice period, which is a *notice* requirement, not an approval duration. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD ITSA) is a conditional future obligation triggered by income thresholds.

claims.claim: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning owners are personally responsible for all of the debts of the business.
claims.snippet: Sole trader businesses have 'unlimited liability' which means owners are personally responsible for all of the debts of the business.

claims.claim: A person can start trading as a sole trader without registering, but must register for Self Assessment if they earn more than £1,000 in a tax year (6 April to 5 April).
claims.snippet: You can start trading straight away without registering. However, you must register for Self Assessment as a sole trader if you earn more than £1,000 in a tax year (from 6 April to 5 April).

claims.claim: Sole traders can choose to register for Self Assessment earlier than required.
claims.snippet: You can choose to register earlier.

claims.claim: After registering, a sole trader will need to submit Self Assessment tax returns.
claims.snippet: After you've registered you will need to submit Self Assessment tax returns.

claims.claim: HMRC works out whether Income Tax and National Insurance contributions must be paid based on profits when the Self Assessment return is submitted.
claims.snippet: When you submit your Self Assessment tax return HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will work out if you need to pay Income Tax and National Insurance contributions based on your profits.

claims.claim: A business must register for VAT if it meets the requirements, and may choose to register early to reclaim VAT on business expenses.
claims.snippet: You need to register for VAT if you meet the requirements. You can choose to register before you meet the requirements if you want to reclaim VAT on business expenses.

claims.claim: Sole traders may need licences or permits, for example to sell food or trade in the street, and should check whether they need business insurance.
claims.snippet: Check if you need: licences or permits, for example to play music, sell food or to trade in the street; business insurance

claims.claim: If a business rents or buys premises it may have to pay business rates, and small businesses can apply for a discount or may pay nothing.
claims.snippet: If you rent or buy a property, you may have to pay business rates. Small businesses can apply for a discount on business rates and some may pay nothing.

claims.claim: Sole traders should keep business records from the start of trading to work out profit or loss for the Self Assessment tax return.
claims.snippet: When you start trading you must keep records. This will help you work out your profit or loss for your Self Assessment tax return.

claims.claim: The guidance does not cover food business registration fees, food hygiene ratings, fire safety, Scotland-specific rules, or Companies House incorporation for Westminster, Manchester, or Edinburgh.

claims.claim: FHIS outcomes are automatically given each time premises are inspected by the local authority, with inspection frequency depending on risk to people's health.
claims.snippet: You'll automatically be given a new FHIS outcome each time your premises are inspected by your local authority. The frequency of these planned inspections depends on the risk to people’s health.

claims.claim: The FHIS business safeguards include request for a re-visit, right to appeal, and right to reply.
claims.snippet: To ensure that the scheme is fair to businesses, it has been designed to include a number of safeguards. These are: Request for a re-visit (when improvements have been made), Right to Appeal, Right to Reply

claims.claim: Businesses must appeal an FHIS Improvement Required outcome in writing within 14 days of being notified, including weekends and public holidays.
claims.snippet: You must make your appeal in writing within 14 days of being notified about your FHIS outcome. This period includes weekends and public holidays.

claims.claim: Businesses are allowed one follow-up re-visit between regular inspections, and the officer will reassess overall standards rather than only the areas worked on.
claims.snippet: You’re only allowed one follow-up visit between your regular inspections... During this re-visit, the officer will look at your overall standards—not just the areas you’ve worked on.

claims.claim: Following a re-visit, the business will be told in writing, either at the time or within 14 days including weekends and bank holidays, of its new FHIS outcome.
claims.snippet: you will be told in writing – either at the time or within 14 days (this includes weekends and bank holidays) – what your new FHIS outcome is.

claims.claim: The appeal result will be notified within a maximum of 7 days from the date the appeal was received by the local authority, after which the FHIS outcome is published online.
claims.snippet: You will be notified of the result of the appeal within a maximum of 7 days from the date that the appeal was received by your local authority. Once you have been notified of the result of your appeal, your FHIS outcome will be published online.

claims.claim: A Right to Reply may be submitted at any time until the next inspection and, after light editing for offensive or inaccurate remarks, is published online with the FHIS outcome.
claims.snippet: There is no deadline for this so you can submit your ‘Right to Reply’ at any time up until your next inspection... Your local authority may edit your comments in order to remove any offensive, defamatory, clearly inaccurate or irrelevant remarks.
